HIGHLIGHT-POSITIVE. Please focus on the parts of the story you like or would be especially interested to see as part of the movie, and use the POSITIVE button to select them.
We open in South Town, a sprawling megacity that feels equal parts Miami and Tokyo.
At a surreptitious gathering of mob bosses and politicians alike, a young man is beaten half to death.
As the mayor of South Town asks who called for this meeting, the handcuffed man smiles. He did.
This is GEESE HOWARD, who breaks his constraints and dispatches the room with a ruthless ease.
This was his ploy to get every key player in the same place. Now, a new kingpin has ascended.
Elsewhere in South Town, two young orphaned brothers TERRY (9) and ANDY (8) sleep in an abandoned building.
They eat handfuls of uncooked rice for dinner and collect cans off of the street for money.
They have the chance to join a gang that steals valuables from unsuspecting beachgoers.
When the gang leader steals sunglasses from a beautiful girl, MAI SHIRANUI (8), Andy returns them to her.
Later, they seek shelter from the rain in an empty karate dojo.
They are scolded by the dojo’s master, JEFF SMITH, but he offers them a meal in exchange for cleaning.
Jeff suspects that the children are orphans and allows them to stay, as long as they go to school and train.
Years pass, and Jeff adopts the boys outright.
He reveals that his real name is ''Bogard,'' but that must remain a secret.
Now teenagers, Terry and Andy run into Mai.
They are both smitten, and they try to impress her, only to run into trouble with her wealthy friends.
A scuffle ensues, and the boys are taken to the police station.
In order to pick them up, Jeff had to use his real name.
Jeff informs them that they need to pack their bags and leave South Town.
Enter Geese Howard, a former rival of Jeff’s who has been hunting him for years.
He walks into the dojo and challenges Jeff to single combat.
Jeff is highly skilled, but cannot withstand Geese’s speed or strength.
Both Andy and Terry try to intervene, but they are no match.
Andy and Terry are knocked unconscious.
Geese kills Jeff and sets the dojo aflame.
Terry wakes up in the neighboring alley and frantically searches for Andy.
He’s distraught, certain his brother died in the fire.
He picks up Jeff's ''King of Fighters'' cap and runs, vowing to return to kill Geese.
Terry trains across the globe - Thailand, Brazil, Russia, China - from top fighters in boxing, muay thai, wrestling, and jiu jitsu.
He also learns discipline and patience.
Years pass, and now an adult, Terry ends his journey learning Tai Chi from the mysterious Tung Fu Rue.
Terry sees an ad for the upcoming King of Fighters tournament in South Town.
The winner gets ten million dollars, but most importantly to Terry, if he enters, he’d get a shot to fight Geese Howard himself.
Terry arrives back in South Town and reconnects with Mai.
They catch up at her favorite noodle shop, where a group of thugs soon enter and pick a fight with Terry.
He easily dispatches them, but fails to notice Mai’s own martial arts skills.
Mai leaves him with the implication that there is something she is holding back.
Terry is staying at a local gym, and after a workout, he hears a mysterious voice in the darkness.
He prepares himself for Geese, but is shocked when Andy steps out.
His brother survived the fire! Andy reinvented himself as ''Andy Luciano,'' an enforcer for Geese who is also fighting in the King of Fighters tournament, all in a ploy to get...
This was the secret Mai was withholding from Terry.
The brothers share a quiet moment together in Andy’s apartment.
Mai later attempts to convince them to drop their plan of killing Geese, but a jealous spark between them drives them apart.
The King of Fighters tournament begins.
Tung Fu Rue serves as Terry’s corner man and hints to Terry a more complicated past relationship between Jeff and Geese.
Andy and Terry move through the rounds in gritty early 2000’s MMA style fights.
Geese watches on, suspicious of both of these mysterious, skilled combatants.
Terry and Andy meet in the championship, and as the opening bell rings, Terry immediately taps out.
Geese realizes these are the Bogards and is furious that his main event has been ruined.
He orders the brothers to be taken to Geese Tower.
In the tower, BILLY KANE, Geese’s main henchman, shows off a captured Mai.
Terry breaks his restraints and a brawl erupts.
Mai handles Billy as the brothers move on Geese.
It all converges at the top of the tower.
Geese gets the upper hand on both brothers and knocks Terry off the edge, seemingly to his death.
As Geese is about to execute Andy, we see Terry on the ledge, semi-conscious.
He hears all his mentors’ voices at once - every fighting master and, most importantly, Jeff’s voice, too - and it lands: stop fighting in anger.
''Fury is fatal.'' Terry climbs up, stunning both Geese and Andy.
This time, he’s calmer, steadier, and more powerful.
Dangling from the tower, our villain, broken and almost amused, chooses death.
He wrenches free of Terry's grip and falls into the darkness below, while Andy grabs his brother's legs to save him from going over with him.
With Geese gone, South Town's criminal empire collapses.
Andy retires the gangster act and opens ''Bogard Martial Arts,'' with Mai at his side.
But deep down, Terry knows he can't stay.
He never could, he's the hungry wolf, the one who keeps running.
The brothers say goodbye at the airport, joking through their emotional parting.
South Town, Andy, and Mai are always his home, but the next adventure is calling.

In the neon-and-diesel sprawl of South Town, drifter TERRY BOGARD steps off an evening bus on the twentieth anniversary of his father's death.
He announces his return by methodically beating five bikers sent to greet him and then starts a one hundred-minute countdown on his watch.
His mission is to end GEESE HOWARD, the kingpin who murdered his adopted father, JEFF, in front of him when Terry was ten.
At the Pao Pao Café, bar owner and old mentor RICHARD MEYER discusses the upcoming King of Fighters tournament, a dark-web death-match streamed to gamblers worldwide.
Geese himself is coming out of retirement to face the night's winner.
He warns Terry not to pursue Geese, and as Terry is about to leave, Meyer gifts him his dad’s old trucker cap.
Terry then stops at his father's grave, where he reunites with his younger brother ANDY, who he hasn’t seen in years.
They both still carry their halves of a domino necklace, a tribute to their father.
Andy is on the same mission as Terry, and he has earned a legitimate slot in Geese’s tournament.
Terry demands to take his spot, demonstrating his mastery of the cyclone kick.
The two brothers begin to fight before they are eventually broken up by Andy's fiancée, MAI SHIRANUI, who tells Terry to earn his own shot at Geese.
Terry then decides to crash Geese's nightclub L'Amor, smashing through the glass window and rampaging through security.
Terry confronts Geese, only to be tased, zip-tied, and loaded onto a helicopter to be dumped into the bay.
Mid-flight, Terry breaks free with a flare gun but chooses to save an innocent passenger instead of killing Geese.
He then dives off of the helicopter into the water below.
As Terry swims to shore, an enraged Geese puts a ten-million-dollar bounty on Terry's head, weaponizing South Town’s gangs, syndicates, and corrupt cops in a violent manhunt.
Terry flees in a brutal gauntlet, beginning with a high-speed bike chase.
Terry escapes, only to be captured by the police, who prepare to execute him.
As Terry sits in the cop car, rival bounty hunters ram him off the pier.
Terry escapes underwater and is rescued by his former girlfriend Blue Mary.
The duo race through the docks of South Town on a jet ski as Geese’s forces pursue.
They reach safety and share a quiet moment over a manatee scarred with the name ''Geese,'' a reminder of Howard’s cruelty and past crimes.
Mary takes an injured Terry to a black market doctor, only to then double cross and drug him with the popular hallucinogen Dragon’s Breath.
Terry is then pursued by Geese’s thug RAIDEN, leading to battle atop a moving train.
As he makes his way to the tournament, he is guided through abandoned tunnels by hallucinations of his ten-year-old self, a wolf, and finally Jeff’s ghost, who tells him the hard...
Terry arrives at Geese’s underground arena with minutes to spare and slips through security disguised as a cop.
In the locker room, an exhausted Andy agrees to name Terry his second, and Tung Fu Rue (Geese's own former master) and Blue Mary join Terry in his corner.
Terry gets implanted with the King of Fighters biochip that provides a live reading to audiences akin to a health bar.
Terry wins his bout against the staff-wielding Billy Kane and earns his chance to fight Geese.
However, during the prematch physical, Geese is diagnosed with a heart condition and bows out of the fight, only to name Andy as his second.
Andy is forced into the ring for a wrenching brother-versus-brother fight, climaxing with Andy dropping Terry.
The crowd, and Geese, believe Terry is dead.
Geese steps into the ring to gloat, and Terry sits up - alive! He reveals that Blue Mary, a former Fraud Unit investigator, hacked his biochip to help fake his death.
Because Geese registered as a fighter and has entered the ring, he now must fight Terry, despite his previous medical exemption.
Simultaneously, Blue Mary hijacks every screen in the arena, exposing Geese's exploitation of South Town.
He used his criminal enterprises to lower prices and then purchase up real estate at a huge discount.
Neighborhoods are shown as ''ACQUIRED,'' including the orphanage where Terry grew up.
The crowd turns against Geese, and he flees.
Terry and Andy battle through Geese's guards up to Howard Tower (aided by an unexpected assist from dancer DUCK KING), splitting up in a rampage to reach the roof.
There, Terry destroys Geese's escape helicopter, and the two finally face off in the rain.
Geese reveals he killed Jeff because Jeff was organizing the dockworkers, threatening his shipping business, but Terry sees the truth beneath it: simple envy of the better man.
Terry unleashes a cyclone kick and sends Geese over the parapet.
Geese catches the edge and Terry, refusing to succumb to the cycle, reaches out with his wounded arm to save him.
Geese refuses to be saved, digging into Terry’s wound and tearing himself free.
As dawn breaks and the hundred-minute clock hits zero, Terry sees a vision of a wolf in the morning light.
Later, the two brothers hang their halves of the domino at Jeff's grave.
Andy invites Terry to stay and rebuild South Town, but Terry, with Blue Mary waiting on a motorcycle, has more miles to ride.
Andy notes the truth of it: Terry came home to kill Geese and ended it trying to save him.
